paragraphs: The stadium was full of red scarves, and every one of them was knitting itself longer while it waited. Arsenal were one player short, and their coach, a tall coat with nobody inside it, pointed at Yellow Duck Sweater. The duck explained politely that it had no arms. The coat nodded as if that were the point: a duck with no arms could never be called for handball. So it walked out onto grass that was cold and springy under its orange feet, the only yellow shirt in a sea of red, and felt the pitch tip gently downhill toward its own goal.

The ball went everywhere the duck was not. Then it came rolling across the slope, and the duck leaned forward the way it leaned into the hill, ran two metres, and met the ball with its whole small body. In the far goal stood the reference duck, tilting its head, and the ball rolled past so slowly that both of them watched it cross the line together. The crowd roared like a jet engine starting. Then the scarves let go of the stands and drifted down in a soft red snowfall, and the duck stood in the middle of it, one yellow spot, while a thin moon balanced on a floodlight like a lost button.

imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: The robot duck in its yellow duckling sweater stands at the mouth of a stadium tunnel at night, facing a tall empty coat with no one inside it that points one sleeve at the duck, while rows of red scarves glow in the floodlit stands beyond. Panel 2: Close-up: the duck tilts its head down toward its armless sides while the empty coat leans over it with a nodding collar, and red scarves in the background curl longer like knitting. Panel 3: The duck walks alone onto a cold green football pitch under floodlights, the only yellow figure on the field, with the grass visibly sloping downhill toward a goal behind it and gray clouds gathering over the stands. Panel 4: A white football rolls down the sloping grass toward the duck as it leans forward and runs to meet it, its orange feet kicking up small bits of turf. Panel 5: Two ducks watch together as the football rolls very slowly over the goal line: the yellow-sweater duck in the middle of the pitch, and a second plain white robot duck with no sweater standing in the goal, tilting its head. Panel 6: The duck stands in the middle of the pitch while dozens of red scarves drift down around it like soft snow, and a thin crescent moon rests on top of a tall floodlight above the stadium. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
